Space
spās
n. (an interval of time or of distance; room; rendering Hebrew yamim and rachoq, Greek chronos and diastema)
Latin spatium, a stretch of room or time. In the Authorized Version the word is almost always an interval of time — a space of three years, of half an hour, to repent.

Biblical Definition

A space is a measured interval. Of time: “I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not” (Rev 2:21); “there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour” (Rev 8:1); Paul “by the space of three years” ceased not to warn the Ephesians night and day with tears (Act 20:31); Sapphira came in “about the space of three hours after” (Act 5:7); Ezra sees that “for a little space grace hath been shewed from the LORD our God” (Ezr 9:8). Of distance: at Jordan “there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it” (Jos 3:4). The beast “must continue a short space” (Rev 17:10).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines space as room; extension; a quantity of time; an interval between points or objects.

expand to see more

SPACE, n. Room; extension; extent; capacity of being occupied.

2. Any quantity of extension; as, the space of a mile.

3. Quantity of time; also, an interval between two points of time; as, the space of a year.

4. A short time; a while.

Key Scripture

Rev 2:21 — "And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not."

Ezr 9:8 — "And now for a little space grace hath been shewed from the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a nail in his holy place, that our God may lighten our eyes, and give us a little reviving in our bondage."

Rev 8:1 — "And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour."

Act 20:31 — "Therefore watch, and remember, that by the space of three years I ceased not to warn every one night and day with tears."

Jos 3:4 — "Yet there shall be a space between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure: come not near unto it, that ye may know the way by which ye must go: for ye have not passed this way heretofore."

Act 5:7 — "And it was about the space of three hours after, when his wife, not knowing what was done, came in."

Modern Corruption

God's delay is taken for God's indifference, when Scripture calls it space to repent and counts every unused day.

expand to see more

Revelation 2:21 is the anatomy of patience. Jezebel of Thyatira was given space to repent, and the sentence ends, “and she repented not.” The modern inference from delay is that God does not mind: the judgment has not come, therefore the thing was allowed. Peter answers that the longsuffering is “not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance” (2Pe 3:9), and Paul answers what the unused space becomes — “despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering… but after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath” (Rom 2:4–5). Space to repent is evidence at the trial when it is not used.

Ezra 9:8 is what a man does with a little space of grace. The remnant has come back, the temple stands, God has given them “a nail in his holy place” — and Ezra's response to the season of favour is to tear his garment and confess the nation's sin. The corruption is the opposite reflex: taking a season of grace as an entitlement, and reading a quiet year as a verdict on one's righteousness. A little space is a loan.

Joshua 3:4 gives space its other direction. Two thousand cubits were to lie between the people and the ark — “come not near unto it” — so that every man could see the way, and so that the holy thing was not handled as common. Uzzah's hand closed the space and he died for it (2Sa 6:6–7). Reverence keeps a distance, and the modern familiarity with holy things, in which nothing is set apart and everything is within reach, is what Joshua 3 was built to prevent.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew yamim (H3117), days, a season; rachoq (H7350), a distance, far off; rega (H7281), a moment; Greek chronos (G5550), time; diastema (G1292), an interval; hemiorion (G2256), half an hour.

expand to see more

Hebrew yamim (H3117) — days, a period; Genesis 29:14, “the space of a month.”

Hebrew rachoq (H7350) — distance, far; Joshua 3:4, two thousand cubits.

Hebrew rega (H7281) — a moment, a little space; Ezra 9:8.

Greek chronos (G5550) — time, a season; Revelation 2:21, Acts 13:21; diastema (G1292), Acts 5:7; hemiorion (G2256), Revelation 8:1.

Usage

"“I gave her space to repent” — patience with a purpose, and a record of how it was spent."

"“For a little space grace hath been shewed” — Ezra's season, and Ezra's confession."

"“A space between you and it” — the distance reverence keeps."
